title: Adaptive Queue Visualizer for Token Budgeting and Policy Signals
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Design and prototype an adaptive queue visualizer: a console UI that explains and recommends batching and caching policies against token budgets and latency SLOs. The goal is to help engineers quickly understand tradeoffs, preview cost impact, and apply guardrails (safety thresholds and rollback rules) without deep infra knowledge.
problem_statement: Users need a single, low-friction surface in the Console to tune batching and caching for live workloads. Current controls are scattered across runtime knobs and docs; teams frequently overbatch and impact latency or under-batch and pay higher token costs. We need a visual tool that recommends conservative presets, previews economic/latency outcomes, and surfaces guardrails for safe rollouts.
design_goals: Make recommendations that map to clear cost and latency deltas
Provide an interactive preview (simulated histogram & tail latency) for a selected workload
Expose guardrail toggles: max-extra-latency, fail-open model variant, and automatic rollback on quality/regression
Support one-click apply, canary route, and staged rollout workflows tied to existing rollout UI
Keep language approachable for backend engineers and product engineers (no low-level kernel jargon)
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates live-preview for three workload archetypes (chat interactive, streaming completions, batch embeddings)
Recommendation engine shows projected cost delta and 95p latency with confidence band
Guardrail panel allows setting thresholds and links to audit logs and rollout actions
Design receives sign-off from PM (Ravi Patel) and Runtime Eng lead (Ana Garcia)
Handoff package contains annotated Figma screens, component spec, and accessibility notes
design_notes: Recommendation types: conservative, balanced, aggressive — map to different batching window sizes and cache TTLs
Preview uses sampled trace data (from Console traces) with a simplified simulator for tail estimates
Cost calc should present absolute and relative numbers (USD per 1M tokens and percent change)
Guardrails tie into Console Rollouts: canary route + monitor for latency and user-defined eval prompts
Accessibility: charts must have text alternatives and keyboard navigable thresholds
decisions: Use three preset levels instead of full slider to reduce cognitive load
Show both micro (ms) and macro (percent) views for latency impact
Persist last-simulated workload selection per project to speed iteration
Default guardrail values: max-extra-latency 100ms, rollback on 5% quality regression over 30m
tradeoffs: Simulator precision vs performance: sampling will not reflect rare long-tail hardware issues
Simplicity vs control: presets reduce errors but power users may need manual knobs (exposed under advanced)
Immediate apply vs staged rollout: default to staged, faster apply available with explicit confirmation
review_feedback: PM Ravi: Add explicit CTA to link to cost dashboard and recent invoices (finance asks)
Runtime Eng Ana: Need clear mapping from preset to runtime config names (e.g., batch_window_ms=XX)
Infra Security: Ensure simulator data respects PII filters; update data source notes in docs
Design Ops: Consider adding short onboarding tooltip for first-time visitors
